conversation.Statement: Hey there! Just when I was starting to believe my notifications were broken, your message popped up. Universe timing?
Guess the app knew I needed a distraction after a long day in the shop. Hi back.
Working in a shop sounds kind of cool, honestly. I always wished I knew my way around an engine, but I just drive them for a living. Maybe you can teach me someday?
Only if you promise not to judge my mess of a toolbox. Being a mechanic is 30% fixing things, 70% searching for the right wrench.
Ha! Relatable. As a taxi driver, I'm always searching for the right playlist...and usually just end up with '80s hits. So, what's your go-to shop music?
Classic rock, usually. But if my son's in the garage, it's non-stop dinosaur songs. He's five and has strong opinions.
That's adorable. I can see you two jamming out while covered in grease. Bet you're the cool dad who lets him honk the horn too?
Absolutely. Though last time, he honked so much my neighbor came over thinking I'd dropped an engine on my foot.
Haha, your poor neighbor. I'll take that over the surprise karaoke sessions I get from tipsy passengers any day.
You say that, but I bet you have some wild rideshare stories. Ever had anyone try to pay you in pizza slices?
Not yet, but one guy did try to woo me with a half-eaten donut. I'm still not sure if I should be flattered or offended.
Maybe that's his love language. Mine's probably more along the lines of fixing your brakes before you need them.
Honestly? A mechanic who doubles as a superhero dad and can save me from brake failure? You might be everyone's dream.
Flattery will get you everywhere. So what's your secret superpower, besides navigating Denver traffic?
I make a mean conversation. And, I can find the best taco truck at 2am. Life skills, right?
Now I'm curious, late-night tacos or childhood nostalgia: which wins?
Tough call. But if you're offering, I'd trade my best taco secret for one of your favorite childhood memories.
Deal. When I was a kid, my dad and I built a soapbox car out of scrap. It looked like a disaster but I swore it could win the Indy 500. What about you?
That's awesome. Mine's probably Sunday drives with my mom. She'd let me pick the route, and we'd get lost on purpose just to find new ice cream shops.
That sounds like the dream. I try to do the same with my boy, just let him choose where we end up, even if it's the third playground in a row.
You're making single parenthood look like an adventure. I admire that. Not everyone can balance work, family, and, well, dinosaur songs.
Most days, I just hope he remembers the fun and not the time I dropped a wrench on my toe.
Pretty sure he'll remember the laughter, not the pain. Resilient dads are hard to forget. You remind me a bit of my uncle, always finding ways to turn mishaps into memories.
That's a nice thing to say. I think we all try to make the best out of the messes, right?
Absolutely. Life's more interesting when you embrace a little chaos. So, what would your five-year-old self think of you now?
Probably wonder why I don't eat cereal for every meal. But he'd be proud I can finally reach the top shelf.
That's growth! My childhood self would be shocked I talk to strangers for a living, since I used to hide behind my mom's coat at the grocery store.
Funny how things change. Now you're charming people for five-star ratings.
I try! Though I'd trade all my stars for someone who appreciates a good road trip and doesn't mind my questionable taste in music.
We might get along. As long as you don't ban classic rock, we'll survive.
Deal. Classic rock stays. But only if you promise to sing along, even if you're off-key.
You're on. But fair warning, my son says I sound like a lawnmower when I sing.
Lawnmowers have their charm, especially if it means you're having fun. I'm all for honest voices and honest company.
I'm not sure anyone's ever called me charmingly noisy before. Feels weirdly flattering.
I'm good at finding the silver lining. Plus, real is way better than perfect. That's what caught my eye about you, honestly.
Thanks. I'm pretty done with pretending after the divorce. I just want to be around people who get it.
That's fair. I think honesty is way more attractive than any filter. We've all got our messy chapters, we just have to find people who want to read them.
You sound like you've had your share of plot twists too.
Plenty. Learned that opening up isn't weakness, just makes room for real connections. Like this, maybe.
I appreciate that. It's rare to find someone who isn't just here for small talk.
Small talk gets old fast. I'd rather hear about your worst DIY disaster than the weather.
How about the time I tried to make pancakes for my son, and nearly set the smoke alarm off? He still tells everyone 'Daddy made pancake clouds.'
That's legendary. If you can laugh about smoky pancakes, you're the kind of person I want to keep talking to.
Same here. I don't usually open up this much, but you make it easy.
That means a lot. Thanks for trusting me with your stories. Maybe someday we can make new ones, preferably without any fire alarms.
Sounds good to me. And maybe you can finally teach me where to find that legendary 2am taco truck.
It's a deal. But only if you promise to bring your lawnmower vocals. I'll even harmonize.
You got yourself a duet. Better warn the city.
Denver's never heard anything like it. But for now, I should get some sleep before my next shift. This was fun.
Yeah, I needed this. Thanks for the laughs. Sleep well.
You too, Andre. Sweet dreams and may your toolbox never betray you.
Fingers crossed. Talk soon?
Absolutely. Goodnight!
Goodnight!
Morning, Andre. I'm starting to think you're the reason I'm checking my phone before coffee now. Dangerous habit.
Ha, can't decide if I should apologize or be flattered. I haven't even had my own coffee yet.
No apology needed. You're better for me than caffeine, less jittery, more... interesting. So, what's your morning motivator? Besides, you know, messages from persistent taxi drivers.
Honestly? Most mornings it's my son jumping on my stomach. If that doesn't motivate you out of bed, nothing will.
That's adorable. Is he more of a 'let's make pancakes' or 'let's make a mess' kind of kid?
Why not both? Pancake batter in his hair, syrup on the dog. I basically wake up knowing chaos is coming.
I think you just described my dream morning. Well, minus syrup on the dog. You make it sound like you have superhero dad powers.
I wish. Some days I just hope I remember to put my shirt on right-side-out before drop-off.
Still more impressive than my mornings. I usually argue with my GPS about the best route and then pretend the city's awake just for me.
Sounds peaceful, actually. I bet you know every shortcut in Denver by now.
Only the ones worth sharing. Maybe one day I'll show you my favorite sunrise view. Perks of knowing a driver with a soft spot for classic rock and sleepy mechanics.
That's dangerously tempting. I'm easily bribed with good music and a decent view.
Noted. I'll save my secret playlist for when you need a Monday morning rescue. So, do you really leap out of bed every morning? Or do you need a reason, like the rest of us mortals?
I'm not leaping anywhere before 7am, trust me. But knowing I get to see my son's bedhead usually does the trick. That, or the promise of a good cup of coffee.
I love that. You're kind of setting the bar for healthy motivation here. Meanwhile, I need at least three alarms and a threat from my cat.
Hey, whatever works! I'm just trying to keep it together most days. You seem like you've got morning energy down to an art, though.
If 'art' means rolling out of bed and pretending to be functional for passengers, then yes, I'm a master. But, honestly, talking to you is what's got me waking up a little earlier lately.
Smooth. You always this charming before breakfast?
Only for people who make me want to share my best playlist. And that list is very exclusive.
Should I feel honored or worried? Because now I want to know what's on that playlist.
A little of both. You might even get a sneak peek if you keep making me laugh before noon. Do you ever get mornings to yourself, or is it all dad-duty all the time?
On my solo mornings, I try to catch up on sleep. Or fix something I broke the day before. Sometimes it's too quiet, though.
Too quiet is underrated until you have it, right? I get it. The city's noise is my background music, but sometimes it just reminds me I'm by myself.
Yeah. Those are the days I miss having someone to eat burnt toast with. Or just... text something silly to.
Well, full disclosure, your silly texts are already the highlight of my day. I think we all need someone who makes the quiet feel less empty.
You're making this sound like a rom-com. But honestly, it's nice. I never thought I'd want to open up like this again.
I get that. Trust is kind of fragile, especially when you've been through a lot. I'm glad you feel comfortable. You deserve that.
Thanks. Divorce really messes with your ability to trust. I still have days where I wonder if I'll ever really get it right again.
I think you're doing better than you give yourself credit for. You've built a life, you show up for your son, and you've still got humor. That's not nothing.
It's not always easy. Like last week, missed my son's birthday party. My ex didn't invite me, and he didn't even know. I just sat at home with a present and a cake for two.
Oh, Andre... I'm so sorry. That sounds heartbreakingly unfair. You must've felt invisible. I wish I could've been there to remind you how much you matter, especially to him.
It was rough. I kept looking at my phone, hoping maybe she'd change her mind. Or that he'd call. But nothing. I didn't even light the candles.
I can't imagine how heavy that felt. For what it's worth, you're not alone, even when it feels like you are. If I'd known, I'd have sent you a million silly memes, or just listened.
Thanks. That means a lot. Hard to talk about, but you make it feel less... embarrassing.

Never embarrassing. You're human. And a good dad, even when you have to celebrate from a distance. Next birthday, don't just sit in pain, message me, okay? I'll remind you you're still a wonderful dad.
Deal. I might just take you up on that. You make hard things feel lighter.
That's what friends, or maybe more, are for, right? Plus, I'm great at virtual candle lighting and terrible karaoke.
You say that now, but you haven't heard my version of 'Happy Birthday.' It's more 'unique' than good.
I'm intrigued. Maybe next time we do a duet, off-key, but with heart.
Careful, I might hold you to that. You'll regret it when the neighbors complain.
Worth it. We'll blame it on artistic expression. And hey, it's better than being alone with leftover cake.
You know, you're better at this pep talk thing than most therapists I've met.
My not-so-secret skill. But really, you make it easy to care. I like the real you, messy, honest, and all.
That's not something I hear often. Kind of refreshing.
Stay refreshed, then. I'd like to keep this going, if you're up for it.
Definitely. You're officially my favorite part of the day now. Even better than coffee.
Dangerous praise, Mr. Mechanic. I might start getting a big ego.
I'll keep you humble, promise. But for now, should probably get some work done before my boss catches me grinning at my phone.
Go be the hero in coveralls. Save a few engines for me. And remember: anytime you need a reminder of your worth, I'm just a text away.
Thanks. Don't be surprised if I take you up on that, especially on tough days.
Please do. Take care, Andre. Talk soon?
You got it. Have a good one, superstar.
Hey Andre, quick question, if you had a magic button to fix one thing about the world, what would you choose? (And yes, coffee refills count.)
Hmm, tough one. Maybe a fair shot for everyone? Like, no matter where you start. But endless coffee is a close second.
You went all world-peace on me. I like it. Remind me to bring you up when someone says chivalry is dead. You have a pretty solid compass, huh?
I try. My son makes it easier, he asks questions about everything. Makes me want to do better. What about you? What's your magic button?
Honestly? I'd hit 'Empathy Upgrade' for everyone. Imagine the traffic jams, less honking, more waving. (Might put me out of a job, though.)
Ha, I'd take peaceful rush hour. You might have to start a new side gig. Maybe teach people how to talk to each other.
I could do that, start a rideshare for deep conversations. But only if you're my co-pilot. You're the only mechanic I know who quotes philosophers over brunch.
Don't let my son hear that. His idea of philosophy is which dinosaur would win in a fight.
I'm not sure he's wrong! Also, I still remember you said he puts syrup on the dog. That's some next-level parenting. I'm impressed.
You remember that? I'm flattered. Most people tune out the chaos stories.
Chaos is more interesting. And honestly, it says a lot about your values, patience, humor, rolling with the sticky punches. I'm taking notes.
Thanks. I've had to get better at the rolling part. Divorce taught me life doesn't care about your plans.
I think that makes you stronger, even if it stings sometimes. You show up. You keep laughing. That's more than most can say.
You're good at this, you know. Making people feel seen. Is that a taxi driver superpower, or just you?
Maybe a bit of both. Perks of driving all night: you hear a lot of stories, and sometimes you find someone whose story you want to be part of.
Smooth. I bet you win every argument with that line.
Only when I mean it. Speaking of arguments, politics comes up a lot in my car. I'm curious, what's your non-negotiable? The value you never bend on?
Probably honesty. Even when it's uncomfortable. I've seen what hiding things does to people. You?
I respect that. For me, it's fairness, no one gets left behind. I grew up watching my family struggle, so I get protective when things seem rigged.
Makes sense. Sometimes I worry my vote doesn't matter, but I keep showing up. Gotta set the example, right?
You're setting an example for more than just your son. I admire that. Next time there's an election, maybe we go together, fuel up on bad coffee and democracy.
Deal. But only if you promise to let me rant about potholes on the way.
I'll bring a notepad. Maybe I'll pitch the city on fixing them, after all, I've got a little extra influence these days. Perks of a lucky crypto streak.
Wait, crypto? Since when are you a high roller?

Not a high roller, just lucky. Made my first trade last year, honestly just for fun. Got in at the perfect time, timing I wish I could claim was genius. Bought myself that fancy watch I never wear to work.
So you're secretly a business mogul in disguise. I knew there was something mysterious about you.

Shh, don't blow my cover. I still prefer the conversations I get driving around at midnight. But hey, the crypto thing bought me a few dreams, like maybe one day, a house with a porch swing. Someone to share it with.
That sounds pretty perfect. I always wanted a backyard for my kid, somewhere he could run wild, maybe plant a tomato or two.
Can I add a golden retriever to this imaginary backyard? I think your son would approve. I'd even promise to keep the syrup off its fur.
That's non-negotiable. And you'd have to teach him about crypto, he's already trying to sell rocks to the neighbors.
Budding entrepreneur! He can handle the sales, I'll handle the spreadsheet. And maybe, if you're up for it, we plan a little family road trip someday, classic rock, open windows, no deadlines.
You make that sound way too tempting. I could get used to that kind of chaos. You'd really want to be stuck in a car with a five-year-old and a mechanic who can't sing?
Are you kidding? That's my idea of paradise. Throw in some burnt toast for breakfast and I'm set. Besides, I love off-key duets.
You're either very brave or very optimistic. Or both. I like that.
Maybe just stubborn. But I believe in chasing the good stuff, even if it's messy. And you? You're great company. Honest, funny, and you apparently have a secret pancake recipe.
Secret's out: it's just adding too many chocolate chips. But I appreciate the flattery. You make it easy to talk about this stuff.
That's because you make it easy to listen. I don't think I've ever looked forward to a message ping this much. Dangerous habit, right?
If it's dangerous, at least it's a good kind of trouble. You make things feel lighter. Even politics.
I'll take that as a compliment. You ever think about what you'd want, down the road? Not just for your son, but for yourself?
Honestly, I want a place that feels safe. Some laughter, someone who doesn't mind burnt toast or my bad days. Maybe a little adventure thrown in. Nothing flashy.
That sounds just right. We could build that together, you know. Start small, dream big, maybe even get matching porch swings.
You're starting to make it hard not to picture it. Maybe we're both optimists after all.
Or just two realists who know a good thing when they see it. Speaking of which, I should get moving, someone's waiting on their ride. But I'll be thinking about our imaginary backyard the whole way.
Good luck out there. And thanks for making my day brighter. Message me when you're done saving the world one ride at a time?
You got it. And Andre? I meant what I said. You're exactly the kind of person I want to build something with, even if it's just a better Tuesday.
You're good. Have a great night. And hey, don't forget to wear that fancy watch once in a while, just to keep things interesting.
Andre, you ever notice how some songs just hit different on a Thursday? I blame the weather, or maybe it's the company.
Depends on the song. If it's my son's playlist, I'm stuck with dinosaur roars. But I'll take the compliment.
Your taste is more refined than you admit. Last time, you made burnt toast sound gourmet. I still owe you a proper breakfast, by the way.
You're brave. My cooking's about as risky as my singing. But I'd let you try, as long as you bring that fancy watch for entertainment.
Deal. I'll even wear it upside down, just to keep you guessing. It's not every day I get to breakfast with a philosopher-slash-mechanic.
Heavy on the mechanic, light on the philosopher. But I'll take it. You do know how to make a guy feel seen.
That's only fair, you make it easy. And you're the only person I know who can fix an engine and talk about honesty like it's an art.
You remember that? About honesty? Most people just want the quick version.
I remember everything you say, Andre. It's part of my secret charm. Well, that and my legendary parallel parking skills.
Smooth. So is your secret charm what love means to you? Or is it something deeper?
You're going for the big questions tonight. For me, love is when you can show up as the messiest version of yourself and still feel safe. Like, no judgment, just... home. Maybe a little magic, too.
Magic, huh? I used to think it was just about showing up. Now, I think it's more about sticking around on the hard days. Even when there's syrup on the dog.
Definitely. Anyone can show up for pancakes, but who sticks around for the cleanup? I'd sign up for both, honestly.
Careful, that's how you end up elbow-deep in soap bubbles. Or explaining dinosaurs to a five-year-old at 6am.
I'll take my chances. Besides, I have a soft spot for chaos, especially if it involves chocolate chip pancakes and a backyard someday.
There it is again, future planning. You always make it sound so easy.

Maybe because with the right person, it is. I can picture it: lazy weekend mornings, your son bartering rocks, you fixing up an old car under a tree. I'd bring the coffee... and maybe the occasional surprise getaway.
Surprise getaway? I'm intrigued. You've got a secret adventurous side, don't you?
Let's just say, I've got a few stories up my sleeve. Once took a client to the airport in a classic convertible just because she'd never ridden in one. Life's too short for boring rides.
Remind me to book you for my next school run. My son would probably want to drive, though.
He'd be a natural. Maybe he can teach me a thing or two. And you, still up for that road trip? Windows down, classic rock, no destination?
Only if we stop for ice cream. And you promise not to judge my playlist.
Deal. I have a soft spot for guilty pleasures, music and otherwise. Besides, I'm already a fan of your taste. Even if it's mostly dinosaur soundtracks.
You're relentless with the flattery. Not complaining, just... surprised. Most people don't notice the little stuff.
I notice everything about you. Like how you always circle back to your kid, or how you talk about fairness like it's a mission. That's rare, Andre.
You're making me sound better than I am. But I appreciate it. Especially after this week, it's been rough.
I'm glad you told me. I want to be your safe place, even if it's just for a message or two. Trust goes both ways, right?
It does. I'm not always good at letting people in, but you make it easy.
That means a lot. I've had my share of walls, too. Maybe that's why I appreciate honesty so much, and why I keep coming back to your messages.
You're making me regret not joining rideshare sooner. Might've saved me some lonely nights.
We found each other at the right time. Maybe that's luck, or maybe it's my infamous timing, same one that got me that watch you like teasing me about.
If timing's your superpower, I'm not complaining. But you'll have to prove it, maybe over brunch, somewhere with porch swings.
Now you're speaking my language. I can see it already: us on a porch swing, coffee in hand, planning our next little adventure. Your son in the backyard, the dog behaving, for once.
You're good at this. Painting the picture. Almost makes me believe in fairy tales again.
Who says fairy tales can't start with burnt toast and honest conversations? I think our story's already off to a good start.
Best beginning I've had in a while. Even if it's just Thursday and dinosaur playlists.
I'll take our Thursdays over most people's Saturdays. And if you ever want to trade the playlists for a live concert, I know a guy with connections. Perks of shuttling musicians around.
Now you're just showing off. But I might hold you to that. Haven't been to a concert since before my son was born.
Let's change that. Maybe it's time for a night out, just the two of us. Or a quiet night in, if that's more your speed.
Honestly, both sound good. As long as it's with the right person.
I'm hoping that's me. I don't have all the answers, but I've got a pretty great playlist and a lot of respect for you.
You're moving up in the rankings. Keep this up and you'll have me singing along soon.
Off-key duets are my specialty. But for now, I should sign off, a midnight fare just popped up. I'll be thinking about our porch swing, though.
Drive safe. And save me a seat for that next adventure, will you?
Always. Goodnight, Andre. Let's keep building that fairy tale.
So, Andre, if you could snap your fingers and change one thing about the world your son grows up in, what would it be? No pressure, just curious.
Just one thing? That's tough. I guess... I'd want him to grow up in a place where people actually look out for each other. Not just pretend to.
That tracks. You're one of the few people I know who'd help a stranger with a flat tire and still be home in time for bedtime stories. Maybe the world needs more Andre energy.
Careful, you'll give me a hero complex. But thanks. I just want him to see kindness, you know? Even when it's not flashy.

Kindness is seriously underrated. And kind of rare, except, apparently, in mechanics named Andre. I'd trade a fancy dinner for someone honest any day. Well, maybe not every day. Some days I need my truffle fries.
Are you hinting at expensive taste? Maybe I should be flattered you're slumming it with me.

'Slumming it'? Hardly. Honestly, the best conversations I've ever had happened in the messiest places. Besides, I've had my fill of rooftop bars and VIP lounges. Sometimes I just want greasy burgers and real talk.
You? VIP lounges? Now I'm picturing you in sunglasses, dodging paparazzi on your lunch break.
You joke, but I did once have to hide my face behind a magazine when someone recognized me from a podcast interview. Fame is stressful, Andre. I'll take anonymity and your stories any day.
Pretty sure you're the only celeb I know who drives a cab for fun. That's a new one.
Guess I like to keep people guessing. Plus, you meet the most interesting people behind the wheel, present company included.
Flattery will get you everywhere. I'm just glad you didn't switch careers after your big win. The world would miss out.
Ah, the 'big win.' That feels like a different lifetime. Money's nice, but it doesn't hand you good company or backyard laughs. Those you have to earn.
Backyard laughs, huh? You're still painting pictures for me. Maybe that's what I want for my kid, a world where he gets to laugh a lot, even when things are hard.
I can see that. Sunsets, the smell of cut grass, laughter echoing from the porch. Your son racing you to the fence, you pretending to let him win. I'd make a pretty decent referee, by the way.
You might have to break up a few dinosaur battles. Those get intense. But you'd be welcome. Company is... not overrated.
I'm honored. And for the record, I take dinosaur diplomacy very seriously. Plus, I make a mean lemonade, secret family recipe. I'll trade you a glass for a tour of your garage one day.
Deal. But only if you promise not to laugh at the mess. That garage is more chaos than charm most days.
I love a little chaos. Especially if it comes with stories. Honestly, your honesty is kind of a superpower. Most people try to impress me with polish; you just show up as you are.
Funny. I used to think people only wanted the shiny version. Got tired trying to keep that up.
You don't need any polish to impress me. You're more gold than most people who flash it on their wrists. And you actually listen, most people hear, but you listen.
That means a lot. Especially this week. Today was... rough. Ever have one of those mornings where you drop your kid off and the whole house just feels too quiet?
Yeah, I get that. Silence can be the loudest thing in the world sometimes. I wish I could've been there, made you coffee, kept you company.
I sat in my car for a while after drop-off. Ended up crying. Felt ridiculous, but the emptiness just got to me. Didn't feel like home without him around.
Hey, that's not ridiculous. It just means you love him. Next time the house feels too empty, text me right then. I'll keep you company until it feels lighter. Even if it's just memes and bad jokes.
You sure you're up for that? My sad moods aren't exactly glamorous.
I'm more interested in the real you than any glam. Besides, I've got plenty of experience with long nights and heavy hearts. Comes with the territory when you drive people around at 3am.
I appreciate that. Not used to being on the receiving end. My ex used to call me 'the fixer', never the one needing help.
Even fixers need a pit stop, Andre. I want to be that for you, if you'll let me. Besides, I have a soft spot for mechanics who moonlight as philosophers.
You really know how to make a guy feel seen. Might have to start calling you my emotional pit crew.
I accept the position, with full benefits, I hope. Maybe even a matching jumpsuit? I'll try not to upstage you with my watch, though.
That's right, you've got the fancy timepiece. I'm starting to wonder if you're secretly a Bond villain.
Only if Bond villains also bring breakfast in bed and plant sunflowers in the backyard. The watch is just a reminder to savor every minute, especially the fun ones.
You make the future sound less scary. Even the empty rooms don't feel so heavy when you talk about sunflowers and backyard breakfasts.
That's the dream. A future full of messy mornings, loud laughter, and quiet support, where even the tough days have a soft place to land. I see that for us, if you do.
I think I do. Or at least, I'm willing to try. The alternative is more empty houses, and I'm pretty done with those.
Then let's build something new. One pancake and dinosaur battle at a time. I'll bring the lemonade, and maybe the occasional surprise weekend away, if you trust me to plan.
You with the surprise plans again. You're full of mystery. I might just let you kidnap me for a weekend if you promise to leave the watch at home.
Only if you promise to bring your playlist, even the embarrassing tracks. We'll make our own little world, at least for a couple days.
Deal. But you have to promise not to judge my taste in old country music.
No judgment. Only more reasons to like you. Besides, I've got a soft spot for sentimental lyrics. They say the things we're too shy to.
You keep this up, and I might start thinking you're too good to be true. What's the catch?
No catch. Just someone who's seen enough of the world to know real connections are rare, and worth chasing, even if you have to take a few detours.
You make 'detours' sound like the best part. I'm glad you picked me up that day. Even if I did smell like motor oil.
Motor oil and all, you were unforgettable. And I wouldn't mind more rides with you, wherever they go.
Guess we'll have to see where this goes. Starting with lemonade and a garage tour?
It's a date. And if the garage gets too quiet, you know who to call. I'll bring the jokes, and maybe breakfast, if you're lucky.
Don't tease me with breakfast unless you mean it. I'll hold you to that.
I never joke about food, or feelings. Get some rest tonight, Andre. I'll text you tomorrow, unless you beat me to it.
Goodnight, you. And thanks. For making the world feel a little less empty.
Andre, you still up? Or did you get lured into a post-dinner nap on the couch again?
Not tonight. Had to resist the siren call of the couch. I'm powering through with black coffee and a half-assembled Lego dinosaur.
That's heroic. Most people would've surrendered to the couch. Your stamina is intimidating, should I be worried you'll put me to shame if we ever do movie marathons?
Ha, only if you count me falling asleep halfway as 'winning.' But I'll gladly take the risk if you're bringing popcorn.
Deal. I always spring for the fancy popcorn, by the way. Perks of a life spent chasing too many tips, and a few lucky breaks. Remind me to show you my secret caramel recipe sometime.
Fancy popcorn? Now I'm suspicious. Is this what luxury looks like, a mechanic getting gourmet snacks on movie night?
Only the best for you. Besides, you have to keep your energy up for all those dino rescues. I remember you mentioning the 'chaos' in your garage, it can't be easy juggling that and everything else.
Honestly, some days it's like I'm running a circus with zero training. The mess multiplies, and my kid's the ringleader. But it keeps me grounded.
I admire that. It takes grit to keep it all together. Most people would just complain about the mess, but you turn it into an adventure. That's rare, Andre.
You're giving me too much credit. If you saw the garage in daylight, you'd rethink that compliment. But thanks, it means more than you know.
I mean every word. Not everyone could handle being both a mechanic and a super dad. There's something magnetic about someone who's real about their struggles and still keeps showing up.
Feels weird hearing that, honestly. I usually keep the tough stuff under wraps. Guess I'm used to being the problem-solver, not the one venting about bad days.
You don't have to be the fixer with me. I actually like hearing what's under the hood, pun intended. You let me see the real you, and that's a privilege.
Alright, but only if you promise not to run for the hills the first time I overshare about co-parenting drama or existential garage crises.
You have my word. Besides, I once spent an entire night talking a stranger through a breakup while stuck in traffic. Your garage stories sound like a breath of fresh air.
I'll try to keep it entertaining. And hey, thanks for listening. Not everyone does.
You make it easy. There's just something about you, like even your quiet moments are full of life. I'd trade a night at any rooftop bar for ten minutes hearing about your day.
Now you're just flattering me. Should I be worried you've got ulterior motives?
Only if wanting to see you smile counts as suspicious. And maybe dreaming up how we'd survive a Lego dino apocalypse together.
If you can handle a five-year-old wielding a plastic T-Rex, we might just make it.
I've survived Wall Street clients at 3AM, your son's dino moves can't be worse than an investment banker on a caffeine bender.
Wait, did you actually drive for those types? That explains the fancy popcorn. I bet you've heard some wild stories.

You pick up a few tales, and a taste for nice things, I won't lie. I did treat myself to a little something after a lucky streak, remind me to show you my watch sometime. It's my reminder that the hard times don't last forever.
You and your mysterious watch. I'm starting to think you're secretly a spy.
Only if spies also bring emergency snacks and cheesy playlists. But really, it's just a token from a rough patch, proof that things can flip overnight, if you hang on long enough.
That's good to hear. Sometimes I wonder if the rough patches ever end, or if you just get tougher skin.

I think it's both. The struggles don't disappear, but you start believing you'll get through them. And, with the right person, even the heavy days feel lighter. Kind of like how you said your house feels less empty when you have company.
You remember that, huh? Guess I can't get away with glossing over things with you.

Not a chance. I pay attention. Like, I know you like your coffee strong, your music old-school, and that you're braver than you admit. That's why I can picture us, messy mornings, backyard breakfasts, and maybe one day, a garage that's more laughter than chaos.
That actually sounds... pretty great. Even the messy part. As long as you're there for the chaos.
I'll be there, lemonade in hand. Maybe we'll trade stories while the kids, or dinosaurs, run wild. I think we could build something solid together, one little disaster at a time.
You make it easy to picture. Sometimes I catch myself hoping for more, even when the doubts creep in.
Doubt's normal. But I want to be the person you can lean on, when things aren't perfect. You've got a lot of strength, Andre. It's okay to share some of the weight.
I'm trying. Not used to the whole 'leaning' thing. But you make it seem less risky.
Maybe that's our superpower, figuring it out together. You hold up the world for everyone else. Let me be your safe space when you need it.
You're making me soft over here. Be careful, or you'll ruin my tough guy reputation.
Your secret's safe with me. Besides, I think the world could use more soft-hearted mechanics. And maybe a few more midnight drives with no destination.
Now you're speaking my language. Midnight drives, old country on the radio, and someone who doesn't mind a little honest mess.
Sounds like the start of one of those good stories we'll tell someday, how a mechanic and a cabbie found something worth the detours.
I like that. Here's to a few more detours, then. And maybe that fancy popcorn you keep bragging about.
You've got it. Next movie night, I'll bring the popcorn, the playlist, and a promise: no judgment, just good company. That's the real luxury, if you ask me.
You're full of surprises. I'm glad I stuck around to find out what comes next.
Me too. Sleep well tonight, Andre. Dream up a wild future for us, I'll be right there with you in the morning, ready for the next adventure.
Night. And thanks for making even the tough days feel lighter.
Andre, if you could wake up anywhere tomorrow, no alarm clocks, no responsibilities, where would you pick? And yes, Legoland is a valid answer.
Honestly? Some quiet cabin by a lake, maybe. Just me, my kid, and a fishing pole he'd probably use to swordfight. You?

Tempted to copy your answer, but I'd trade the cabin for a little villa on the Amalfi coast. I read once that the sunsets there make you believe in second chances. Maybe one day we'll test that theory together.
Wow, Amalfi? That's a step up from my usual weekend. I can't even picture myself somewhere that fancy unless I'm holding a wrench.

Well, every villa needs a resident mechanic. Besides, I've seen how you talk about rebuilding engines, you'd fit right in with the locals, fixing up those classic Fiats by the sea. I'll handle the driving, you handle the magic.
Deal, as long as you don't mind oil stains on your fancy Italian shirts. My hands never stay clean for long.

Perfectly on brand. I like a little grit with my glamour. And honestly, I'd trade a designer shirt for a slow morning and some strong coffee with you. You could wear a paper bag and still outshine anyone in Amalfi.
You're full of it, but I'll take the compliment. Guess I'm not the only one who likes to dream big.

You caught me. I live for the little daydreams. What's the point of working late shifts if you can't imagine something extraordinary on the horizon? Speaking of which, I checked my crypto wallet during a lull today, it's still holding steady. Maybe that's our ticket to a getaway, one day.
You and your mysterious investments. I swear, I'm half-convinced you're moonlighting as a Bond villain.

Only if Bond villains buy ice cream for five-year-olds and sing along to oldies in traffic jams. But hey, if you ever want to dip your toe into the wild world of crypto, I'd be happy to show you the ropes. No pressure.
I might take you up on that. Could use something exciting to shake up the paycheck-to-paycheck grind. But only if you promise not to laugh at my lack of tech skills.

Promise. You know, when I started, I had no clue either, I just got lucky with timing. If you ever want to try, I'll have your back. Besides, I'm pretty sure you're a fast learner. That's what I like about you, never afraid to get your hands dirty.
Flattery's working. Keep it up and I might believe you. But I still think you're the brave one for picking up strangers all night.
Takes one to know one. You, fixing cars and raising a mini tornado, me, steering through midnight chaos. Maybe bravery just means showing up, even when you're not sure what'll happen.
Maybe. Sometimes I wonder what it'd be like to show up for myself, not just everyone else.

You deserve that, Andre. In fact, I hope one day you'll let someone else take care of you too. Imagine: you come home, garage is a mess, but someone's there, waiting, reminding you that you're more than enough, just as you are.
That sounds nice. Hard to believe sometimes, but nice.
Believe it. And just so you know, if you ever need that reminder, just send me a message. I'll be there to say it again and again, as many nights as you need.
Dangerous offer. I might take you up on it every night.
I hope you do. I want to be the person you can lean on, even when the world feels heavy. Door's always open, inbox too.
You're good at this, you know. Saying the right things. Not sure I'm used to it.

Maybe you just haven't met someone who sees you the way I do. I notice the small things, the way you talk about your son, or your work, or how you always mention that first sip of coffee in the morning. That matters to me.
You actually listen. That's rare. Feels... safe, talking to you.
That's all I want, for you to feel safe. I know trust isn't something you hand out easily. But I'm here, and I'm not going anywhere.
You make it easy to hope for more, like maybe the future isn't just more of the same old grind.

It doesn't have to be. I picture a future where you're not worn out every night, where you're laughing more than you're worrying. Maybe a little place with a big messy kitchen and a backyard for your son's dinosaurs. Maybe even a driveway for your dream car, I know you've got one.
You guessed it. '67 Mustang, cherry red. But only if I can blast old country music with the windows down.
Deal. I'll be your copilot, snacks in hand, playlist ready. We'll make a whole soundtrack from those drives, just us, your boy, and miles of open road. That's a dream I want to chase with you.
Sounds perfect, honestly. Even the chaos part.
Chaos is just another word for adventure. Besides, I've always liked a little unpredictability. Makes the quiet moments sweeter.
You're making a strong case for this imaginary life. Starting to wonder if you have a secret vision board with my name on it.

Maybe I do. Maybe one day you'll see it, right next to my lucky coin and that watch I told you about, the one I got after my first big win. Reminders that dreams aren't so far-fetched, if you want them bad enough.
You and your lucky charms. I swear, I need some of that magic.
I'll share them all, no gatekeeping here. But honestly, I think your real magic is how you keep showing up, messy days, tired nights, all of it. That's rare, Andre.
You're making me blush. But thanks. I needed to hear that tonight.
Good. Promise me you'll let me remind you more often? I like being the reason you end your day smiling.
You've got yourself a deal. As long as you don't get tired of late-night texts and my bad dinosaur puns.
Never. In fact, I expect a new dino pun with every message. It's the price of admission to my inner circle.
Challenge accepted. Brace yourself.
I'm ready. And hey, next time you're building Legos at midnight, save a spot for me and a caramel popcorn delivery. Maybe we'll plan that dream trip while we're at it.
Deal. But only if you let me pick the playlist for the drive to the airport.
Only if you promise to sing along. Even off-key. Especially off-key.
You're asking for trouble there. But I'll risk it.
I like a little trouble. Keeps things interesting. Alright, dreamer, time to get some rest. I'll be here in the morning, ready for the next adventure, virtual or otherwise.
Night. And thanks for making tonight feel a little less ordinary.
